title: Android from the foundation
intro: Lifecycle, process death, ANRs, frozen screens: most of Android's hard parts come from a handful of ideas. This course builds them from the ground up, one small puzzle at a time, with pictures that move, until the rules stop being rules and start making sense.
how: Each puzzle starts with a problem Android had to solve, then gives you one building block, a picture to remember it by, and a diagram that plays itself (or step through it yourself). It ends with three questions: answer them all correctly to unlock the next puzzle, so no gap carries forward. Code names with a dotted underline open the real Android or Linux source: hover or tap them.

modules.title: Module 1: The ground floor
modules.blurb: What a running app is, who's in charge of the phone, and the four characters every later puzzle uses: your app, the kernel, the town hall and the post office.

modules.title: Module 2: Apps and their code
modules.blurb: Why apps can't touch each other, how they still talk, what's inside an APK, and how an app starts so fast.

modules.title: Module 3: The machinery
modules.blurb: Inside a Binder call, the main thread's queue, and why one slow line freezes the screen.

upcoming.title: Module 4: Screens and their lives
upcoming.topics: Context, rotation, saved state, process death, tasks and the back stack.

upcoming.title: Module 5: Work without a screen
upcoming.topics: Services, broadcasts, ContentProviders, Doze and WorkManager.

upcoming.title: Module 6: Threads, coroutines and Flow
upcoming.topics: What really runs where, cancellation, cold and hot streams.

upcoming.title: Module 7: Pixels and performance
upcoming.topics: How a frame is drawn, Compose internals, memory and leaks.
